Spanish = modern spelling (accents, b/v, h, x/j, joined words; no rewording and no change of word order), each message keeps the text as printed in the public-domain edition in orig.es (shown in the app as an optional ‘original spelling’ line). Editors' interjections are removed; nothing is taken from the 1981/82 or 2003 editions or their notes. verified=false: checked against the archive.org full text, a last check against the page images is still to do. en · ko translated from the Spanish for this app. Replies and talks are written by this app, not by the recipients.

note.ko: 1775년 1월 마드리드에 온 고야는 왕립 산타 바르바라 태피스트리 공장에서 짤 그림의 밑그림(카르톤)을 그리기 시작했어요. 직조공들이 보고 그대로 짜는, 벽 크기의 큰 유화예요. 첫 밑그림들은 왕세자의 사냥 별장 식당에 걸 사냥 장면이었어요. 이 짧은 편지는 사라고사의 마르틴에게 썼어요. 1868년 판은 편지 속 ‘프란시스코’가 바예우라고 적어요.
note.en: Goya came to Madrid in January 1775 and began painting cartoons for the Royal Tapestry Factory of Santa Bárbara: large oil paintings, the size of a wall hanging, that the weavers copied. His first cartoons were hunting scenes. He wrote this short letter to Martín in Zaragoza; the 1868 edition notes that the ‘Francisco’ of the letter was Bayeu.
note.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 8 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa ; image: see plate.imageSource

why.en: One of the first tapestry cartoons Goya painted in Madrid, in 1775.

messages.es: Infinitas gracias, y muchas más, por las expresiones de amistad que te merezco, y no dudes que, si había de cansar a alguno, sería a ti.
messages.en: Endless thanks, and many more, for the words of friendship I have from you; and don't doubt that if I had to trouble anyone, it would be you.

note.ko: 1777년 봄, 고야는 큰 병을 앓았어요. 무슨 병이었는지는 편지에 적혀 있지 않아요. 이 편지는 회복한 뒤 마르틴에게 썼어요. 같은 해 고야는 〈양산〉 같은 밝은 밑그림을 그렸어요. ‘작은 밭(campicos)’은 그가 늘 꿈꾸던 고향의 조용한 삶이에요.
note.en: In the spring of 1777 Goya was seriously ill; the letter does not say what the illness was. He wrote this to Martín once he had recovered. The same year he painted bright cartoons such as ‘The Parasol’. ‘Campicos’, little fields, stand for the quiet life at home he always dreamed of.
note.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 8 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa ; image: see plate.imageSource

why.en: A tapestry cartoon from the year of his illness, made for the dining room of the Prince and Princess of Asturias.

messages.es: Sr. D. Cornelio Vandergoten: De orden del señor don Francisco Sabatini se servirá vuestra merced de entregarme el cuadro pintado por mi mano que representa El ciego tocando la guitarra y varias gentes oyéndole, para el fin que vuestra merced sabe.
messages.en: Señor Don Cornelio Vandergoten: By order of Señor Don Francisco Sabatini, please be so good as to hand over to me the picture painted by my hand that shows The Blind Man Playing the Guitar and various people listening to him, for the purpose you know of.

note.ko: 이 글은 친구에게 쓴 편지가 아니라, 왕립 태피스트리 공장의 책임자 코르넬리오 반데르고텐에게 보낸 짧은 요청서예요. 궁정 건축가 프란시스코 사바티니의 지시로, 자기가 그린 밑그림 〈기타 치는 눈먼 사람〉을 내어 달라고 해요. ‘아시는 그 일’이 무엇인지는 쪽지에 적혀 있지 않아요. 크루사다 비야아밀이 1870년에 펴낸 『고야의 태피스트리』가 이 쪽지를 실었어요. ‘Vmd.’는 ‘vuestra merced(귀하)’의 줄임으로, 오늘날 usted 의 옛 꼴이에요.
note.en: This is not a letter to a friend but a short request to Cornelio Vandergoten, director of the Royal Tapestry Factory. On the orders of the court architect Francisco Sabatini, Goya asks for his own cartoon ‘The Blind Guitarist’ to be handed back to him; the note does not say what ‘the purpose you know of’ was. Cruzada Villaamil printed it in ‘Los tapices de Goya’ (1870). ‘Vmd.’ abbreviates ‘vuestra merced’, the old form behind today's usted.
note.source: G. Cruzada Villaamil, Los tapices de Goya (Madrid, 1870), p. 122 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/lostapicesdegoy00villgoog ; image: see plate.imageSource

messages.es: Querido Martín: Con Antonio Ibáñez te envío un juego de las obras de Velázquez que he grabado, que ya sabrás que tiene el Rey; no te las he enviado antes porque no se supiera que aquí he tenido mil enredos con ellas.
messages.en: Dear Martín: With Antonio Ibáñez I'm sending you a set of the works of Velázquez that I have engraved, which, as you'll know, belong to the King; I didn't send them before so that no one would know I've had a thousand troubles with them here.

note.ko: 1778년 고야는 왕궁에 걸린 벨라스케스의 그림들을 따라 동판에 새겨 판화로 펴냈어요. 왕궁에 가지 않고는 볼 수 없던 그림을 많은 사람이 볼 수 있게 한 일이에요. 그해 마드리드 신문에 판매 광고도 실렸어요. 그림은 그 판화를 위해 고야가 그린 〈바쿠스의 승리〉(술꾼들) 소묘예요. 사바티니는 왕궁 공사를 맡은 궁정 건축가였어요. 편지 뒷부분의 거친 농담 한 구절은 싣지 않았어요.
note.en: In 1778 Goya etched a series of prints after the paintings by Velázquez in the royal palace, so that many people could see pictures that otherwise only the court saw; they were advertised in the Madrid paper that year. The picture is Goya's drawing of ‘The Triumph of Bacchus’ (The Drunkards) made for the print. Sabatini was the court architect in charge of the palace works. A crude joke later in the letter is left out.
note.source: A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 10 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192 ; image: see plate.imageSource

messages.es: Si estuviera más despacio, te contaría lo que me honró el Rey y el Príncipe y la Princesa, que, por la gracia de Dios, me proporcionó el enseñarlas cuatro cuadros, y les besé la mano, que aún no había tenido tanta dicha jamás.
messages.en: If I had more time I'd tell you how the King and the Prince and Princess honoured me; by the grace of God I was able to show them four pictures, and I kissed their hands, a joy I had never had before.

messages.es: Y te digo que no podía desear más en cuanto a gustarles mis obras, según el gusto que tuvieron de verlas y las satisfacciones que logré con el Rey, y mucho más con Sus Altezas, y después con toda la grandeza, gracias a Dios, que yo no merecía, ni mis obras, lo que logré.
messages.en: And I tell you I couldn't have wished for more, as far as their liking my work goes, judging by the pleasure they took in seeing it and the satisfaction I had with the King, and much more with Their Highnesses, and afterwards with all the grandees, thank God; neither I nor my work deserved what I got.

messages.es: Pero, chiquío, campicos y buena vida: nadie me sacará de esta opinión, y más que ahora empiezo a tener enemigos mayores y con mayor encono.
messages.en: But, my boy, a few little fields and a good life: no one will talk me out of that, all the more now that I'm beginning to have bigger enemies, and angrier ones.

note.ko: 1779년 1월, 고야는 왕궁에서 카를로스 3세와 아스투리아스 왕세자 부부(훗날의 카를로스 4세와 마리아 루이사)에게 그림 네 점을 보여 드리고 손에 입을 맞췄어요. 궁정 화가를 꿈꾸던 서른두 살 화가에게 큰일이었어요. 그림 속 〈그릇 장수〉는 그 무렵 공장에 넘긴 밑그림이에요. 편지 속 ‘프란시스코’는 처남 프란시스코 바예우예요. 1916년 베루에테 판이 괄호로 이름을 덧붙였어요.
note.en: In January 1779 Goya showed four pictures at the palace to Carlos III and the Prince and Princess of Asturias, the future Carlos IV and María Luisa, and kissed their hands: a great moment for a painter of thirty-two who hoped to serve the court. ‘The Crockery Vendor’ is a cartoon he delivered to the factory at about this time. The ‘Francisco’ of the letter is his brother-in-law Francisco Bayeu; Beruete's 1916 edition adds the name in brackets.

note.ko: 1780년 5월, 고야는 마드리드의 산 페르난도 왕립 미술 아카데미 회원이 되었어요. 같은 해 사라고사 필라르 대성당의 둥근 천장 하나를 맡아, 고향에 가서 일할 채비를 했어요. 마르틴과 사라고사에서 지낼 집 이야기를 나누던 무렵의 편지예요. ‘티플레(tiple)’는 소리가 높은 작은 기타예요.
note.en: In May 1780 Goya became a member of the Royal Academy of San Fernando in Madrid. That year he was also given one of the domes of the basilica of the Pilar in Zaragoza to paint, and got ready to work in his home town; this letter comes from the time he and Martín were discussing a house there. A ‘tiple’ is a small, high-pitched guitar.

lines.en: Martín, I'm looking for a small house.
What do you need in your house?
A table and five chairs.
Great. I have a table.

speak.en: But I repeat: // if you think it is the right thing, / do it.
speak.ko: 그래도 다시 말하지만, / 네가 보기에 맞다 싶으면 그렇게 해 줘.

note.ko: ‘집은 여자의 무덤’이라는 말은 아내 호세파가 한 말을 고야가 옮긴 거예요. 1780년대 그만한 집안의 결혼한 여자는 삶의 대부분을 집 안에서 보냈어요. 그래서 이 한 줄은, 두 사람이 사라고사에서 알아보던 집을 호세파가 어떻게 보았는지 알려 줘요.
note.en: ‘The house is a woman's grave’ is Josefa's own remark, reported by Goya. In the 1780s a married woman of her class spent most of her life indoors, so the line tells us how she saw the house they were looking at in Zaragoza.
note.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 11 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa ; image: see plate.imageSource

why.ko: 집 밖, 나무 아래에서 노는 여인과 아이들을 그린 고야의 밑그림이에요. 호세파의 말과 나란히 보면 좋아요.
why.en: Goya's cartoon of women and children out of doors under the trees: worth seeing next to Josefa's words.

replies.es: Lo siento. La casa no es alegre.
replies.en: I'm sorry. The house isn't cheerful.
